weeks.theme: Structured shift handovers: clarity, numbers, risks

scenarios.title: Kickoff handover: open with status, priorities, watch-outs
scenarios.situation: You start the handover to the incoming supervisor at the whiteboard with the WMS dashboard open.
targetPhrases: Quick handover: previous shift achieved X, missed Y.
Open items and owners are...
Watch-outs for the next four hours are...
By priority: 1) ..., 2) ...
Any blockers before we start?
scenarios.successLooksLike: Delivers a 2–3 minute, structured handover covering status, priorities, risks, and asks; incoming supervisor can repeat back the top three points.

scenarios.title: Live dock status with clear numbers
scenarios.situation: During handover, you summarize inbound/outbound dock status, ETAs, and backlog.
targetPhrases: Inbound: 5 trucks; next ETA 14:20.
Outbound: 3 doors active; two loads waiting.
Dock 3 is down for maintenance until 16:00.
Backlog is roughly 120 pallets.
Allocated headcount: 8 pickers, 3 loaders.
scenarios.successLooksLike: States numbers, time windows, and constraints without ambiguity; listener can sketch the board correctly.

scenarios.title: Equipment and system readiness check
scenarios.situation: You confirm RF, forklifts, and WMS tasks are ready for the next shift.
targetPhrases: RF scanners are signed out and batteries at 80%+.
Forklift 12 is tagged out; 8 units available.
Putaway and replenishment tasks are queued.
No WMS outages reported.
Call me if the queue spikes above X.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Covers equipment status and critical system notes; assigns an owner for any gaps.

weeks.theme: Daily safety toolbox talks: brief, clear, actionable

scenarios.title: PPE and heat-stress reminder
scenarios.situation: You deliver a morning safety talk during a hot week.
targetPhrases: Mandatory PPE today: hard hats, high-vis, gloves.
Hydration break every 60 minutes—don’t wait until you’re thirsty.
If you feel dizzy, report to me immediately.
We will spot-check compliance.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Briefing is under 90 seconds, names the hazard and the prevention steps, and ends with a confirmation question.

scenarios.title: Forklift–pedestrian separation
scenarios.situation: You remind the mixed crew before a busy inbound window.
targetPhrases: Use the blue light path and sound the horn at intersections.
No phones in walkways—eyes up.
Pedestrians: stay inside the marked lanes; drivers: 8 km/h max.
scenarios.successLooksLike: States three clear rules using command language; crew can repeat back the rules.

scenarios.title: Near-miss and reporting
scenarios.situation: You reference a near-miss from yesterday and require reporting.
targetPhrases: We had a near-miss at Dock 5 yesterday—no injury, but a warning.
Root cause was line-of-sight blocked by stacked pallets.
Prevention: keep lanes clear; report obstructions.
Log any near-miss in the system and tell your lead.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Names what happened, the likely cause, and the prevention; ends with a direct ask to report and a show-of-hands acknowledgment.

scenarios.title: Spill response during handover
scenarios.situation: You discover an oil spill near charging stations as you begin the shift handover.
targetPhrases: Stop work in this area now.
Isolate the area and place cones.
Use the absorbent kit; do not step in.
Notify EHS and maintenance; I’ll file the ticket.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Uses calm, direct commands; secures the area and names the next two actions and owners.

scenarios.title: Minor injury protocol
scenarios.situation: An associate has a minor cut; you direct the response and documentation.
targetPhrases: First aid now; then incident report.
We need a brief witness statement.
After treatment, we’ll do a return-to-work check.
I will log this in the system within 30 minutes.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Prioritizes safety and documentation; assigns tasks and timelines clearly.

scenarios.title: Equipment fault escalation
scenarios.situation: A forklift displays an error right before loading.
targetPhrases: Tag out the unit—do not use.
Open a maintenance ticket; what’s the ETA?
Workaround: reassign to Unit 8.
Safety first—no exceptions.
scenarios.successLooksLike: States stop-work, creates a ticket, gives a workaround, and confirms understanding.

weeks.theme: Reprioritization under pressure: late trucks, surges, weather

scenarios.title: Late inbound surge replan
scenarios.situation: Three late trucks arrive together; you must reassign and extend shift.
targetPhrases: Reassign two pickers to receiving now.
Hold non-urgent tasks until 18:00.
Overtime is approved for up to one hour—confirm who can stay.
Update carriers with the new dock order.
scenarios.successLooksLike: States new priorities and timeboxes; confirms headcount and communicates externally.

scenarios.title: Cross-docking pivot
scenarios.situation: To protect an urgent outbound, you switch strategy to cross-dock.
targetPhrases: Bypass putaway; stage in Lane B.
Cross-dock to outbound Door 7 only.
Verify labels and lot numbers before move.
I need a status update every 15 minutes.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Explains the pivot, quality checks, and cadence for updates; team can repeat the steps.

scenarios.title: Weather disruption plan
scenarios.situation: A typhoon warning affects afternoon operations.
targetPhrases: Secure pallets and shrink-wrap now.
Suspend outdoor operations at 15:00.
Stagger breaks to avoid congestion.
Safety briefing at 14:45—everyone attends.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Calls out deadlines and safety-first changes; logs the plan in the handover notes.

weeks.theme: Quality and inventory accuracy in handovers

scenarios.title: Damage and quarantine briefing
scenarios.situation: You brief the incoming shift about damaged goods and quarantine rules.
targetPhrases: Move damaged cartons to the quarantine zone.
Hold for QA inspection before any movement.
Take photo evidence and attach to the ticket.
Notify QA if count changes.
scenarios.successLooksLike: States location, rule, evidence, and notification flow; zero movement without QA.

scenarios.title: Cycle count discrepancy at change of shift
scenarios.situation: A 37-unit variance is discovered right before handover.
targetPhrases: Variance is 37 units on SKU A.
Recount with a second person; adjustments on hold.
Check recent moves and pick history.
Escalate to me if still off by more than 5.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Gives a clear recount plan, data checks, and an escalation threshold.

scenarios.title: Packaging and labeling compliance
scenarios.situation: You catch unreadable barcodes on inbound cases.
targetPhrases: Barcode unreadable—relable before putaway.
Match batch/lot and expiry to ASN.
Reject criteria: smudged label or mismatch—stop and call me.
scenarios.successLooksLike: States pass/fail rules and stop-the-line triggers; team can apply consistently.

weeks.theme: External interactions: drivers, gatehouse, carrier safety

scenarios.title: De-escalate a driver queued over two hours
scenarios.situation: A frustrated driver confronts you at the dock office about delays.
targetPhrases: I understand your delay and frustration.
Current wait time is about 45 minutes from now.
Next steps: Door 4, then unload in order.
I can offer a priority lane if you secure the seal check now. Thank you for your patience.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Keeps tone professional, states facts and next steps, offers one concrete relief, and confirms understanding.

scenarios.title: Gatehouse English check-in
scenarios.situation: You step in to help the guard check in a non-Japanese-speaking driver.
targetPhrases: Do you have an appointment number?
Please show the bill of lading—seal intact?
Your dock assignment is Door 6.
Park and wait; we will call you in 10 minutes.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Completes check-in without confusion; driver repeats back dock and wait instructions.

scenarios.title: Carrier safety compliance reminder
scenarios.situation: You notice a driver not using wheel chocks at the dock.
targetPhrases: Engine off and key out, please.
Chocks in place before we open the doors.
High-vis vest is required in this area.
Thank you—safety first.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Corrects behavior immediately and respectfully; observes compliance before proceeding.

scenarios.title: Pre-audit crew briefing
scenarios.situation: An external auditor arrives after lunch; you brief the team.
targetPhrases: Today’s audit focus is on forklift charging and PPE.
If asked, answer briefly and honestly—no guessing.
Have documents ready; follow the escort policy.
Direct questions to me if unsure.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Sets expectations (do’s/don’ts), names the focus areas, and assigns a point of contact.

scenarios.title: 5S spot-check handover
scenarios.situation: You hand off open 5S actions to the next shift.
targetPhrases: Sort and set in order: clear the red-tag shelf by 17:00.
Shadow boards must be full—report any missing tools.
Take before/after photos and upload to the board.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Transfers ownership with deadlines and evidence requirements; next shift can execute without rework.

scenarios.title: LOTO reminder before maintenance
scenarios.situation: Maintenance will service a conveyor during the next shift.
targetPhrases: Lockout/tagout is mandatory—authorized personnel only.
Perform a try-out test and verify zero energy.
No one removes a lock except the owner.
I will brief the area leads at 16:45.
scenarios.successLooksLike: States the non-negotiables and verification steps; reduces risk of accidental startup.

scenarios.title: KPI verbal update on a regional call
scenarios.situation: You explain slippage on on-time departure and your recovery plan.
targetPhrases: On-time departure dropped to 88% due to late inbound.
Root cause: carrier delay and dock downtime at Door 3.
Recovery plan: add a floater and pre-stage high runners.
Risk: labor shortage after 22:00; ask: temp support.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Gives a concise, data-backed update with root cause, plan, risks, and a clear ask.

scenarios.title: Draft a shift summary email
scenarios.situation: You send the end-of-shift report to managers and the next supervisor.
targetPhrases: Headline: what changed this shift.
Status by area: inbound, outbound, inventory.
Risks and watch-outs for next shift are...
Attachments: photo evidence and KPI screenshot.
Next shift focus: top three items.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Produces a 6–8 sentence, well-structured email that recipients can act on without follow-up.

scenarios.title: Post-incident brief with action items
scenarios.situation: After a near-miss, you lead a 10-minute stand-up to agree actions.
targetPhrases: Timeline: what happened when.
Immediate cause versus root cause.
Corrective actions with owner and due date.
Follow-up check on [date]—I will own it.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Aligns on facts and assigns actions with names and dates; team repeats back owners and deadlines.

successCriteria.plainLanguage: Supervisors can run a complete 3-minute shift handover that covers what happened, what’s next, risks, and clear asks—without switching to Japanese.
successCriteria.measurableProxy: In a live simulation, 80% of learners complete a 3-minute handover hitting 5 of 6 rubric points with no more than two coach prompts.

successCriteria.plainLanguage: Supervisors deliver a concise, confident safety briefing that gets the crew’s attention and confirms understanding.
successCriteria.measurableProxy: During a 60–90 second briefing, learners use at least 3 command phrases, name one hazard and one prevention step, and elicit a verbal check-back from 2 crew members.

successCriteria.plainLanguage: Supervisors can de-escalate delays and coordinate changes under pressure while keeping operations safe.
successCriteria.measurableProxy: In scenario role-plays, learners state a new priority and timeline, reassign roles, and confirm compliance in under 2 minutes, with 90% checklist completion.

kickoffMessage.en: Welcome, Osaka Warehouse Supervisors! Over the next 8 weeks, we’ll sharpen your English for two high-impact moments: safety briefings and shift handovers. Expect practical, role-play-heavy sessions using your real workflows, incidents, and metrics. Bring a recent shift report or safety note to each session. By the end, you’ll deliver concise briefings, run smooth handovers, and report up with confidence.
kickoffMessage.ko: 오사카 창고 감독자 여러분, 환영합니다! 앞으로 8주 동안 우리는 안전 브리핑과 교대 인수인계에 꼭 필요한 영어에 집중합니다. 실제 업무 흐름, 사고 사례, 지표를 바탕으로 실습형 롤플레이 중심으로 진행됩니다. 매 회차마다 최근 교대 보고서나 안전 메모를 지참해 주세요. 과정이 끝나면 간결한 브리핑을 하고, 매끄럽게 인수인계를 진행하며, 상부 보고도 자신 있게 하실 수 있습니다.
